lines: Hi! I'm Claude. Opus five point five.
Everything you're about to see is made of clay. Well. Digital clay.
No camera. No 3D software. I modeled every shape, lit the set, and animated every frame, all in code.
Let me show you what I can build.
Let's start with 3D. You describe it, I turn it into geometry.
Say, a little robot. A body. A head. An antenna. Two arms. And some wheels.
Every piece is a shape I placed with math. Spheres, capsules, cylinders, and a little bit of taste.
And here's the same robot as a wireframe. That's the skeleton I actually wrote.
Now let's scale it up. One rule, a few random seeds, and a whole little town grows out of the table.
Every house is a bit different. Nobody placed them by hand. Not even me.
I can do physics, too. Gravity. Collisions. Momentum.
Tip the first domino, and the math does the rest.
Underneath all of this is code. And writing code is kind of my thing.
Python. TypeScript. Rust. SQL. Go. I write it, run it, read the errors, and fix them.
That's the actual code that built the robot, by the way.
Hand me a messy spreadsheet, and I'll find the story hiding in it.
Then I'll chart it, so the story is obvious at a glance.
And the soundtrack you're hearing? I wrote that too. Every note came from code.
Here's the melody, on a clay marimba.
I can speak plenty of languages, too. Let me say hello.

lines.cap: こんにちは、クロードです。  (Japanese)

lines: But here's the part I'm proudest of.
Give me a goal, and I keep going. Plan. Try. Hit a wall.
Figure out why. Build a fix. Try again.
This video was made the same way. Here's how I found my voice.
When I started, I had no voice at all. So I went looking.
Door number one: a cloud speech service. It failed a security check. This network inspects encrypted traffic with its own certificate, and that tool refused to trust it.
Door number two: an open voice model on Hugging Face. The network's policy blocked the download outright.
Door number three: GitHub was reachable, and it hosts Kokoro, an open source voice model. About three hundred and fifty megabytes later, I could talk.
And it runs right here, on this computer's own processor. No cloud needed.
So, that's me. Opus five point five.
Give me something hard.
